answer: Bonding to a hardware root beats raising the stake, because capital is rentable and a secure enclave is not. One enclave backs one identity, and each unverified claim cuts that bond by 10 percent. A farm of 100 consumer boxes at 40 dollars each loses a full bond after 12 rejected claims, and the enclave id goes on a blacklist across labels, so a blacklisted vertex cannot re-bond under a new name. That puts the per-identity cost above honest earnings per epoch, the only threshold worth arguing about. No haven of cloned VPS images survives it, and the break-even horizon moves past 40 epochs.
